item.title: This still needs a lot of work
item.content:encoded:
I like the idea behind this SCP, but so far none of the rewrites have caused it to suddenly become interesting.

I think the problem is that we're trying too hard to revise the effect instead of just giving it a new one. Frankly, an SCP that imitates other SCPs is fundamentally boring, and the note at the end where the scip asks for ideas just sounds like a cry for help from the author. We need to pump some life into this bastard.

I recommend the insertion of some experiment logs where D-class personnel get carted into the tunnel and we get either screaming or abrupt radio silence, make the tunnel a bit scarier. I also think that 903 needs to start producing more original concepts for SCPs, something other than imitations or blatant copies.

Who's with me?

item.title: Thoughts
item.content:encoded:
• I don't like the use of the word "old". If necessary, give the date it was constructed in, but "old" is very subjective.
  • "The resulting incident is most likely what caused SCP-903 to be in its current condition." « I don't like the end of this sentence — something about how the word 'be' is mentioned, maybe. Perhaps "to develop anomalous properties." would be better.
  • "walls, but the exact method how this works is unclear." « Same there. Maybe go with "walls. It is unclear how this occurs.".
  • "After an indeterminate amount of time, SCP-903 will suddenly activate the monorail cart on its own." « should be something like "After a varying period of time, SCP-903's monorail cart will activate on its own.".
  • "different effects and abilities." « I feel like the Foundation would just abbreviate it to "different anomalous properties" or something like that.
  • "they have a "lifespan" of approximately two hours before crumbling into dust" « I think this could be phrased to avoid the use of the scare-quoted "lifespan", and something about crumbling into dust bugs me.
  • "However, besides their source" « Reads confusingly. Just cut it to "However,".
  • There is no such thing as an objectively bad joke.
  • "Ton" is an ambiguous unit of measurement. Go with "tonne", which is metric (1000 kg).
  • I don't know how I feel about the tomatoes and blue lady cigarette tests. On one hand, they make sense in context. On the other hand, they feel a little derivative (although this could be that I'm immediately familiar with the SCPs in question).

Overall, though, I think I like this enough for an upvote. It's definitely a substantial improvement.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
A monorail tunnel? We can be just like Black Mesa!

Anyways, what I think is that this article suffers from a certain lack of description, or even implied description. We are told that the monorail seems to have absorbed the effects (there's a problem here;how does the tunnel know what's anomalous? How do the effects get absorbed when they are so varied in nature? Never mind answering those, they're just nitpicks and are solved by simple suspension of disbelief) but we aren't really shown what happens, besides a few imploding personnel here and there. I'm not asking you to spoil the mystery by spelling everything out, but at least hint at some of the effects that have gone through and mixed with others. For this article, just showing us the output won't do, I think. (It's a fine line, though. Too much in the other direction and the artifact's mechanism is laid bare, exposing it as a mental construction instead of a subject of investigation. )

I seem to have rambled a bit. I think it's the result of typing slowly from a cell phone. Short version: show us some evidence.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I love the picture for this one, and the idea of an SCP monorail tunnel appeals to me a lot. That said, there are a few things I dislike here.

The first, and the least important, is that we already have a Site-XX utility tunnel SCP.

Second, some of the writing seems a tad heavy handed. Easily fixable.

The main problem I have here, though, is the SCP's effect. By which I mean its lack of an effect of its own. By borrowing random effects from other SCPs, this article simultaneously crosspollinates several articles and detracts from the creativity of the article itself. The end result is, to me, a sub-par article that feels forced, as though the author just wanted to write an SCP for the sake of writing one, with no particular inspiration.
The core noun is good (anomalous monorail tunnel + awesome picture), but the verb of the article (random effects from other SCPs) doesn't seem strong enough to stand on its own.
That last addendum, I think, is a step in the right direction. Perhaps if that aspect were developed further, this concept could grow into a solid SCP.
